newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Aussie Home move could increase PUMA supply.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Aussie Home move could increase PUMA supply.

text.p: Macquarie Bank's Ltd securitisation arm PUMA Management Ltd said it may have to increase its issuance programme if the Aussie Home Loans venture into business loans proves successful.

"It depends on how successful this initative is. If this results in a dramatic increase in volume, then it will flow through to greater levels of bond issuance," Tony Gill, managing director at PUMA, told Reuters.
Aussie Home Loans, which has a strategic tie-up with PUMA, said earlier on Monday that it was now offering business loans at 7.49 percent, undercutting the traditional bank lenders.
"We expect it will be successful, and if that is the case it will result in increased bond issuance," Gill said.
Last week, PUMA said its bond issuance for 1997 would be A$3.0 billion, a percentage of which is expected to raised offshore, compared with A$1.3 billion in 1996.
Gill said that PUMA's bond issuance is driven by the volumes of loans written, plus or minus its decisions on warehousing.
"So there is not necessarily a direct corrolation between the volumes written and the securities issued because we have some substantial warehouse lines that we also use," Gill said.
PUMA is due to price a A$500 million four tranche bond issue on Thursday.
